request.prompt: Standing on the tide stair itself, at eye height, looking along the wet black rock toward the cave mouth in the headland. Foreground: broken stone treads slick with seawater, weed in the cracks, a shingle landing to the left where the swell runs up. Middle: the dark opening of the sea cave, low and wide, water standing in its floor. Above and behind, the underside of the headland and one corner of the watchtower's stonework against the night sky, its lamp window dark. A wooden oil cask wedged in the rocks near the cave mouth. No figures, no text.
request.style_note: The Tidewatch, in the same hand throughout: cold night palette of wet black rock, grey weathered stone and a green-black sea, painted concept art with visible brushwork, moonlight as the only warm value, no saturated colour anywhere. Each image is ONE single full-frame view of that place, filling the frame edge to edge: never a sheet, never a grid, never a panel, never an inset or a caption.
